correctness.rationale: Starting from the published exact band inequality, division by the leading \(a^4k^4\) term leaves \(2\sin(kL_2)\sin(kL_3)\) plus a uniform \(O(k^{-2})\) remainder. On a rational period, simple zeros require \(O(k^{-2})\) neighborhoods and simultaneous zeros require \(O(k^{-1})\) neighborhoods, so their energy-weighted total discrepancy is \(o(R^2)\) up to momentum \(R\). The remaining square-wave correlation has mean zero if one reduced integer is even and \(1/(pq)\) if both are odd. A fresh exact interval computation independently reproduced the formula for 83 coprime pairs with \(p,q\le11\).
correctness.risk: The theorem is confined to the exactly collapsed connecting edge and gives only limiting density, not finite-energy error rates.

final_claim: For the collapsed-edge degree-four ring chain of Baradaran, Exner and Tater with \(L_2/L_3=p/q\) in lowest terms, the asymptotic positive spectral-energy density is \(1/2\) if one of \(p,q\) is even and \(1/2+1/(2pq)\) if both are odd; in particular the asymmetric ratio \(1:3\) has density \(2/3\), correcting the published universal asymmetric value \(1/2\).
limitations: Rational arc ratio theorem; irrational ratios retain the generic one-half mean.
